sources.title: Covariance-Calibrated Prediction-Powered Inference
newly_inspected_units: S2.11 Proposition S2.5 and one-step corollary
sources.established: Same first-order-efficient limits can coexist with very different conditional finite-design risks. Regular fixed-dimensional logistic existence and numerical accuracy are also treated under stated pilot and weight conditions.
sources.effect_on_our_claim: Generic first-order versus finite-sample differences and generic pilot/global-solution diagnostics are not new claims. The comparison must concern our specified convex corrected loss and proportional-dimension existence boundary. The observable-reference identity is not itself a sampling theorem.
sources.remaining: No claim of theorem-by-theorem equivalence exclusion beyond the inspected units; no complete full-paper rereading asserted

sources.title: On the existence of maximum likelihood estimators in a multinomial choice model under positivity constraints
sources.established: MLE existence under positivity constraints, additional monotonicity conditions, and an operational multinomial criterion are within the stated scope.
sources.effect_on_our_claim: Multinomial existence criteria and finite-iteration/boundary distinctions cannot be claimed generically new. Our current loss uses unconstrained coefficients and labelled subtraction; exact correspondence requires the unavailable full theorem statements.
sources.full_text_status: Subscription preview; no purchase or institutional-access bypass attempted

sources.title: Calibeating Prediction-Powered Inference
sources.established: Post-processing prediction scores, linear-calibration equivalence to PPI++, and the classical general AIPW estimating-function class are treated. The general moment result assumes a regular consistent solution.
sources.effect_on_our_claim: Prediction recalibration and fixed-dimensional variance equivalence are not innovations here. The current observable path is a controlled score-preserving diagnostic, not a proposed superior calibrator or a new AIPW class.
